newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA OFFERS NATIONAL SHRS.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA OFFERS NATIONAL SHRS.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Friday that it had offered to sell a part of the government holding in National Development Bank Ltd to foreign investors at 260 rupees per 10-rupee share.

"The government converted 27.5 million debentures to 18.33 million ordinary shares under an early conversion agreement and has offered 16.5 million shares to foreign investors," Mano Tittawella, director general of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), told Reuters.
"The issue has been oversubscribed with firm offers for 35 million shares," Tittawela added.

National Development Bank and joint lead managers Jardine Fleming and Lehman Brothers had completed a road show for the issue in Singapore, Hong Kong, San Francisco, New York, London and Edinburgh in the last 10 days, where the price was arrived at through a "book building" process, Tittawella said.
"The issue attracted over 50 investors with 34 percent demand from Asia, 31 percent from UK and 27 percent demand from the the U.S.," an NDB statement from London said.
Many of the subscribers are first time investors in the Sri Lankan market, it added.
